question: Why does a centrifugal pump usually need priming?
options: Priming increases the motor voltage so that the starting current is lowered
Priming lubricates the bearings and the mechanical seal before the first start
It cannot create enough suction to lift liquid when its casing is full of air
Priming cleans the impeller of fouling before the pump takes up the load
explanation: Self-priming arrangements (for example vacuum pumps on bilge or ballast pumps) remove air so the pump can draw liquid.

question: Why must a positive displacement pump have a relief valve?
options: To prime the pump by letting air out of the casing before the liquid arrives
Its discharge pressure rises until something fails if the discharge is blocked
To cool the pump bearings by returning part of the liquid to the suction line
To control the pump speed by opening when the motor current rises too far
explanation: Never start a positive displacement pump against a closed discharge valve unless a relief valve is fitted.

question: Cavitation in a pump happens when:
options: The local pressure at the suction falls below the vapour pressure of the liquid
The liquid is very cold, so its viscosity rises and the flow into the impeller falls
The discharge valve is fully open and the pump delivers a very large flow
The pump runs at low speed with the suction valve partly closed in cold weather
explanation: Vapour bubbles collapse violently, causing noise, vibration, impeller erosion and loss of performance.

question: To avoid cavitation, the net positive suction head available (NPSHa) must be:
options: Zero
Greater than the NPSH required by the pump
Equal to the discharge head
Less than the NPSH required, with a margin for the losses in the discharge pipe
explanation: Raise suction head, reduce suction losses or lower liquid temperature to increase NPSHa.

question: Non-return valves in bilge suction branches are fitted to:
options: Prevent sea water or bilge water flowing back into compartments
Measure the bilge level in each compartment and send the reading to the control room
Reduce fuel consumption by stopping the bilge pump when the suction is empty
Increase the pump flow rate by keeping the suction pipe full at all times
explanation: SOLAS requires bilge arrangements that prevent water passing from the sea or from one compartment into another.

question: A gear pump is a:
options: Jet pump
Rotary positive displacement pump
Centrifugal pump with a single impeller and a volute casing around it
Axial-flow pump
explanation: Gear pumps are widely used for lubricating oil and fuel oil transfer.

question: Running two identical centrifugal pumps in parallel mainly:
options: Doubles the head at the same flow, as the two heads add together in the pipe
Increases the flow rate at about the same head
Reduces the flow rate
Has no effect
explanation: Pumps in series add head; pumps in parallel add flow.

question: Compared with gland packing, a mechanical seal:
options: Needs a steady drip of liquid to work, which is collected in the gland drain
Must be tightened daily
Cannot be used on centrifugal pumps
Leaks much less and needs no regular adjustment
explanation: Mechanical seals must never run dry, as heat quickly damages the faces.

question: Under SOLAS, the emergency fire pump on a cargo ship must be:
options: Driven by the main engine through a clutch so that it starts whenever the engine runs
Used only in port when the main fire pumps are shut down for maintenance work
Located outside the machinery space and have an independent power source
Located in the main engine room, close to the main sea water cooling pump
explanation: This ensures water for firefighting if a fire disables the machinery space and main fire pumps.

question: By the pump affinity laws, if a centrifugal pump's speed is doubled, the power absorbed becomes:
options: Unchanged
About 2 times greater, in proportion to the increase in the speed of the shaft
About 4 times greater
About 8 times greater
explanation: Flow is proportional to speed, head to speed squared and power to speed cubed: 2³ = 8.

question: Screw pumps are commonly used on board for:
options: Emergency fire pumping with sea water, as they are self-priming with large flow
Pumping exhaust gas to the economiser at a high pressure from the turbocharger
Transferring high-viscosity fluids such as heavy fuel oil and lubricating oil
Pumping refrigerant from the receiver to the evaporators of the provision plant
explanation: They give smooth, pulse-free flow and handle viscous liquids well.

question: If the oily water separator's 15 ppm alarm is activated, the system must:
options: Switch off the alarm
Automatically stop overboard discharge or return the water to the bilge or tank
Increase the discharge rate so that the bilge tank is emptied before the alarm resets
Discharge anyway and log it later, since the alarm shows only a short peak
explanation: MARPOL Annex I requires an automatic stopping device and a recorded 15 ppm alarm.

question: The main purpose of a sea chest strainer is to:
options: Increase pump suction pressure by removing the air and gas from the sea water
Measure the temperature of the sea water and send it to the cooling water controller
Stop debris and marine growth entering the sea water cooling system
Prevent oil pollution by separating oil from the sea water entering the pump suction
explanation: Clean strainers regularly. Change over to the standby sea chest before opening one.

question: Water hammer in a steam line is mainly caused by:
options: A fully open steam trap, which lets steam flow into the condensate return line
High boiler water pH, which causes foaming and carry-over into the steam line
Too much superheat, which makes the condensate in the line boil off suddenly
Condensate collected in the line being driven at high speed by steam
explanation: Warm up lines slowly, open drains first and keep steam traps working.

question: Why is it important to keep the suction pipe of a centrifugal pump airtight?
options: Air leaks reduce suction and can make the pump lose prime
Air leaks increase the discharge pressure by compressing the air in the casing
Air leaks only affect the motor
Air improves cooling
explanation: Check suction joints, valve glands and strainer covers when a pump fails to deliver.

question: In a centrifugal pump, the impeller gives the liquid velocity, and the volute casing:
options: Seals the shaft where it passes through the casing, using the gland or seal
Primes the pump
Filters the liquid
Converts much of that velocity into pressure
explanation: The gradually widening volute slows the liquid down, raising its pressure.

question: A positive displacement pump should be started with its discharge valve:
options: Open
Removed
Half closed
Closed
explanation: Starting against a closed discharge causes a rapid pressure rise; the relief valve is only a last safeguard.

question: Bilge suctions in the machinery space are fitted with mud boxes or strainers in order to:
options: Measure the bilge level and start the pump automatically when it rises in the well
Separate oil from water before the bilge water reaches the oily water separator
Heat the bilge water to help the separation of the oil in the oily water separator
Stop debris from blocking or damaging the bilge pump and valves
explanation: Strainers and mud boxes must be cleaned regularly and their covers properly refitted.

question: Ballast pumps on most ships are of the:
options: Screw type for heavy fuel
Reciprocating hand-pump type
Centrifugal type, with a priming arrangement
Gear type, with a relief valve to protect the pump from overpressure
explanation: Centrifugal pumps handle large volumes of water at moderate head.

question: A butterfly valve is:
options: A quarter-turn valve with a rotating disc, often used on large-diameter water pipes
A safety valve for air receivers
A screw-down valve for steam only, with a stem that rises as it is opened
A non-return valve for fuel oil lines, which has a hinged disc held shut by a spring
explanation: Butterfly valves are compact and light, but less suitable for fine throttling of high-pressure fluids.

question: Gland packing on a pump shaft should normally be adjusted so that:
options: Liquid runs freely from the gland in a steady stream, to cool the shaft sleeve
A slight drip of liquid continues, to lubricate and cool the packing
No liquid at all leaks, so that the gland is dry and the shaft is not cooled
The shaft cannot turn by hand when the pump is stopped, to show the packing is tight
explanation: Over-tightened packing overheats and scores the shaft sleeve.

question: An ejector (eductor) creates suction by:
options: A reciprocating piston that draws the liquid into a cylinder and pushes it out
A rotating impeller driven by an electric motor, which throws the liquid outwards
Gravity only, by lowering the discharge of the pipe below the level of the tank
Using a high-velocity jet of water, steam or air, with no moving parts
explanation: Ejectors are used for bilge and ballast stripping and to create vacuum in fresh water generators.

question: A fuel oil overflow tank is provided to:
options: Store lubricating oil which has been drained from the engine sump and filters
Hold sludge from the purifiers until it is landed ashore or burned in the incinerator
Collect oil that overflows from tanks during filling or transfer
Store fresh water from the evaporator for use in the boilers and the cooling system
explanation: Overflow tank level alarms warn the crew before oil can escape through vents.

question: A hydrophore (pressure set) fresh water system works by:
options: Keeping an air cushion in a pressure tank, with the pump on pressure switches
Using the main sea water pump to supply the water through a pressure reducing valve
Using gravity from a tank on the mast, so that the pressure is steady at all taps
Running the pump continuously at full speed, with the surplus returned to the tank
explanation: If the air cushion is lost, the pump starts and stops too frequently.

question: Expansion bellows or loops are fitted in steam pipelines to:
options: Drain condensate from the low points of the line when the steam is shut off
Allow the pipe to expand and contract with temperature changes without overstressing
Reduce the pressure of the steam before it reaches the heaters and the turbines
Increase the flow of steam through the line by reducing friction in the long straight pipe
explanation: Without them, thermal expansion could crack flanges, valves or pipe supports.

question: The most common cause of hydraulic system failures is:
options: Contamination of the oil by dirt, water or air
Too much clean oil in the tank, which causes the pumps to run too slowly
Low ambient humidity
Using the correct filters
explanation: Good filtration and regular oil analysis are key to reliable hydraulic systems.

question: A Bourdon tube pressure gauge works because:
options: A float rises in the liquid and moves the pointer through a link at the dial
A spring is compressed by the temperature of the liquid inside and moves the pointer
An electric current changes with the pressure and moves the needle of the gauge
The curved tube tends to straighten as the pressure inside it rises, moving the pointer
explanation: Gauges should be fitted with isolating cocks so they can be changed without stopping the system.

question: Running a centrifugal pump fitted with a mechanical seal while it is dry:
options: Has no effect
Cleans the impeller
Can quickly overheat and damage the seal faces
Improves the seal's life by letting the faces run in without liquid film
explanation: The seal faces depend on a thin film of liquid for lubrication and cooling.

question: Duplex filters are used in fuel and lubricating oil systems so that:
options: Filters never need cleaning, since one side always holds the dirt for the other
Two different oils can be mixed in the filter chamber before they reach the engine
The pressure is doubled across the filter, so that finer particles are removed
One side can be cleaned while the other stays in service, without stopping the flow
explanation: The changeover valve must be operated carefully to avoid air locks or loss of pressure.

question: Before opening a pump for maintenance, you must:
options: Open the casing while it is still under pressure, to see whether the liquid is clear
Close and secure the suction and discharge valves, isolate and lock off the motor, and drain it
Only stop the motor at the local switch, then remove the casing cover to inspect the impeller
Leave the valves open to drain the system, then start dismantling the casing at once
explanation: A permit to work and checks for residual pressure and temperature are also needed.

question: A centrifugal pump is normally started with its discharge valve closed or nearly closed because:
options: It cannot run with the valve open, because the motor would trip on starting
It prevents cavitation completely at the impeller eye by raising the suction pressure
Power demand is lowest at low flow, which reduces the motor starting load
It increases the suction lift of the pump and lets it draw liquid from a lower tank
explanation: The valve is opened gradually once the pump is up to speed; running too long at shut-off overheats the liquid.

question: An air vessel on the discharge side of a reciprocating pump:
options: Smooths out pressure and flow pulsations
Increases the suction lift
Removes air from the liquid
Primes the pump by storing liquid for use when the suction is empty
explanation: It acts as a cushion, absorbing peaks and releasing liquid during the suction stroke.

question: Bilge suction valves are usually of the screw-down non-return type in order to:
options: Allow oil to be pumped to the sea by opening the suction against the bilge pressure
Allow each suction to be closed, while preventing back-flow into the compartment
Increase the pump capacity by allowing a second suction to be opened at once
Reduce the noise of the pump
explanation: This stops flooding from spreading between compartments through the bilge system.

question: A globe valve is preferred to a gate valve when:
options: The flow needs to be throttled or finely controlled
A full, unrestricted bore is needed for the flow of a viscous liquid, such as fuel
Only on/off service is needed
The valve must be quarter-turn
explanation: The flow changes direction through a globe valve, which gives good control but more pressure drop.

question: A gate valve is best used:
options: For throttling the flow when it is half open, to give fine control of the pressure
As a non-return valve, to stop liquid from flowing back through the pipe when the pump stops
As a pressure relief valve, set to open when the line pressure is too high
Fully open or fully closed, giving a straight-through flow with little pressure drop
explanation: Throttling with a gate valve causes vibration and wear of the gate and seats.

question: Under the ISO 14726 pipe colour code, the basic identification colour for sea water pipes is:
options: Blue
Yellow
Green
Brown
explanation: For example, fresh water is blue and fuel oil is brown.

question: Spray shields or anti-splash tape around fuel oil pipe flanges are fitted to:
options: Insulate the pipe from heat loss and keep the temperature of the oil constant
Prevent fuel spraying onto hot surfaces if a joint leaks
Identify the pipe contents
Reduce vibration
explanation: Fuel spray onto hot exhausts is a leading cause of engine room fires.

question: For a centrifugal pump running at constant speed, as the flow rate increases, the head developed:
options: Becomes zero immediately
Increases
Stays exactly the same
Decreases
explanation: This is shown by the pump's head-flow characteristic curve.

question: Wear rings in a centrifugal pump are fitted to:
options: Reduce internal leakage from the discharge side back to the suction
Seal the shaft where it passes through the casing, in place of the gland
Hold the impeller on the shaft against the thrust and stop it from moving axially
Prime the pump by keeping a ring of liquid in the casing when the suction is empty
explanation: As wear rings wear, the clearance increases and pump efficiency falls.

question: Bilge and ballast centrifugal pumps are often fitted with a vacuum pump or air ejector to:
options: Clean the strainers by reversing the flow through them from time to time
Increase the discharge pressure by adding a second stage to the pump casing
Remove air from the suction line so the pump can prime itself
Cool the pump bearings by drawing a flow of air through the bearing housing
explanation: Automatic priming units allow the pump to draw liquid from below its own level.

question: Tank air pipes are fitted with automatic closing heads (for example ball floats) on deck to:
options: Release oil vapour into the engine room when the tank is being filled with fuel
Measure the tank level and send the signal to the remote tank gauging system
Let air in and out of the tank but stop sea water entering in heavy weather
Prevent air entering the tank at all, so that the tank always stays under a vacuum
explanation: Air pipes prevent over-pressure or vacuum in the tank during filling and emptying.

question: In a central cooling system:
options: Sea water circulates through every engine cooler in turn, as in a conventional open system
Fresh water cools the sea water in the central cooler, which is then used for the engines
No sea water is used at all, as the ship is cooled by air coolers on deck
Sea water cools a central cooler, which cools the fresh water circuit of the engine coolers
explanation: This limits sea water piping to a small part of the system, reducing corrosion and fouling.

question: Compared with shell-and-tube coolers, plate heat exchangers:
options: Are always larger than shell-and-tube coolers for the same heat load, and heavier
Are compact and efficient and easy to open for cleaning, but rely on many gaskets
Cannot be cleaned without cutting open the plates, so that they must be replaced as a set
Work only with steam on one side, and cannot be used for water or oil coolers
explanation: Gasket failures may cause leaks between circuits, so pressure tests are done after maintenance.

question: Sacrificial zinc or soft iron anodes are fitted in sea water coolers to:
options: Protect the cooler from galvanic corrosion
Increase heat transfer by coating the tubes with a layer of conductive metal
Measure the water flow
Filter the sea water
explanation: The anode corrodes instead of the more valuable cooler metals and must be renewed when wasted.

question: A fresh water generator works under vacuum so that:
options: Sea water boils at a low temperature, using waste heat such as engine jacket water
The water is sterilised by the pressure, and the salts are removed with the brine
Salt is removed by freezing the sea water at a low temperature in the shell
No heating is needed at all, since the vacuum alone will boil the sea water in the shell
explanation: Typical boiling temperatures are around 40-60 °C.

question: When the salinometer of a fresh water generator detects high salinity in the distillate:
options: The distillate is sent to the drinking water tank anyway, with a warning shown on the panel
The generator stops the main engine so that no more distillate is made at sea
Sea water is added to dilute it until the salinometer shows a normal reading
An alarm sounds and the distillate is dumped instead of being sent to the storage tanks
explanation: High salinity may be caused by priming in the evaporator or a leaking condenser.

question: Drinking water produced or stored on board is usually disinfected by:
options: Adding sea water in small amounts to bring up the mineral content of the water
Chlorination or UV treatment, with residual chlorine checked regularly
Heating it to 40 °C in the tank for one hour and then storing it in the pressure tank
Filtering through cloth only, to remove the particles, then adding a little salt
explanation: Drinking water tanks should also be cleaned and inspected at regular intervals.

question: Most shipboard sewage treatment plants work by:
options: Mixing it with ballast water and discharging both at the same time at sea
Simple storage in a tank until the ship is more than 12 miles from land
Aerobic biological treatment, followed by settling and disinfection
Burning the sewage in the incinerator before the ash is landed ashore with the garbage
explanation: Air blowers keep bacteria alive; chlorine or UV disinfects the effluent.

question: Under SOLAS, emergency steering drills must be carried out at least:
options: Once every three months
Once a week
Only at dry-docking
Once a year, at the same time as the annual survey of the steering gear
explanation: The drill includes direct control from the steering gear compartment and the communications procedure with the bridge.

question: A compound gauge on a pump suction is used because it can show:
options: The pump's speed
Both vacuum and positive pressure
Only very high pressures
Only temperatures, since it has a thermometer scale next to the pressure scale
explanation: Suction pressure can be below or above atmospheric depending on the tank level.

question: Most ballast water treatment systems use:
options: Freezing the ballast
Adding oil to the ballast
Filtration followed by UV treatment or electrochlorination
Heating the ballast to boiling point in the ballast tank before it is discharged
explanation: They must be type-approved to meet the D-2 performance standard.

question: A progressive cavity (mono) pump must not run dry because:
options: It loses its prime permanently and the whole pump must be replaced by the maker afterwards
Its relief valve will open and let the liquid back to the suction while it is dry
Its impeller will overspeed and damage the drive shaft and the coupling quickly
The rubber stator depends on the pumped liquid for lubrication and quickly overheats
explanation: These pumps are often used for sludge and sewage.

question: In machinery spaces, an emergency bilge suction is normally connected to:
options: The fuel oil transfer pump, because it is the only pump with a connection to the bilge
The largest available power pump other than the bilge pumps, usually the main sea water pump
The fresh water hydrophore pump, because it is the only pump with a bilge connection fitted
The sewage pump, because it is designed to handle solids and dirty water in suction
explanation: This gives a large pumping capacity if the machinery space floods.

question: The head developed by a centrifugal pump varies with impeller speed approximately as:
options: The square root of the speed
The speed itself
The cube of the speed
The square of the speed
explanation: By the affinity laws, flow varies with speed, head with speed squared and power with speed cubed.

question: The operating point of a centrifugal pump is found where:
options: The pump's head-flow curve meets the system resistance curve
The motor current is lowest
The NPSH required is zero
The suction and discharge pressures are equal and the flow through the pump is zero
explanation: Throttling a valve changes the system curve and moves the operating point.

question: In a lube oil cooler, the oil pressure is usually kept higher than the sea water pressure so that:
options: Heat transfer is doubled, because the oil film inside the tubes is thinner
The sea water pump uses less power when the oil pressure is higher than the water
A tube leak lets oil into the water rather than sea water into the oil
The cooler needs no anodes if the oil pressure is higher than the water pressure
explanation: Sea water in the lube oil would cause corrosion and bearing damage.

question: In an electro-hydraulic steering gear, the variable-delivery pump:
options: Delivers a fixed flow in one direction only, and the rams are moved by valves
Supplies fuel to the main engine, and also drives the rudder through a gear train
Changes the amount and direction of oil flow to the rams, under the hunting gear
Runs only when the rudder is amidships and stops once the rudder is hard over to one side
explanation: When the rudder reaches the ordered angle, the hunting gear returns the pump to no delivery.

question: SOLAS requires the main steering gear to move the rudder from 35° on one side to 30° on the other in not more than:
options: 60 seconds at any speed, with the rudder moved from 35° on one side to 35° on the other
28 seconds, at the deepest seagoing draught and maximum ahead service speed
28 seconds with the ship stopped, and not at the deepest draught and service speed
10 seconds at half speed, with the rudder moved from 35° on one side to 35° on the other
explanation: The auxiliary steering gear must move the rudder from 15° on one side to 15° on the other in 60 seconds at half speed or 7 knots.

question: Under SOLAS, the steering gear must be checked and tested by the ship's crew:
options: After arrival in port only
Once a month at sea
Only at the annual survey, when the surveyor is on board to witness it
Within 12 hours before departure
explanation: Tests include the main and auxiliary steering gear, remote controls, power units, rudder indicators and alarms.

question: New or repaired pressure piping is commonly hydraulically tested to about:
options: 1.5 times its design pressure
Its normal working pressure only
Ten times its design pressure
Half its design pressure
explanation: Class rules set the exact test pressure for each pipe class.

question: Overboard discharges from spaces below the freeboard deck must normally be fitted with:
options: A gate valve on deck, with a handwheel that is locked when the ship is at sea
Only a blank flange and a manual valve that is kept closed by the engineering watchkeeper
A simple open pipe, if it is above the load line and fitted with a flap outside
An automatic non-return valve with a positive means of closing from above the freeboard deck
explanation: This is required by the Load Line Convention to stop sea water flooding back into the ship.

question: A centrifugal pump discharging against very low system resistance, with its discharge valve wide open, may:
options: Run far out on its curve and overload its motor
Need no NPSH
Produce its maximum head
Stop pumping completely, as the head would fall to zero and the impeller stall
explanation: Power absorbed by a centrifugal pump rises with flow, so very high flow can trip the motor overload.

question: Which change will increase the NPSH available at a pump suction?
options: Heating the liquid, which raises its vapour pressure and so increases the margin
Partly closing the suction valve
Raising the liquid level in the suction tank above the pump
Using a smaller, longer suction pipe
explanation: Higher static head, cooler liquid and lower suction losses all increase NPSHa.

question: A minimum flow (recirculation) line on a centrifugal pump is provided to:
options: Increase the pump's maximum flow by returning part of the liquid to the suction
Prevent the liquid overheating when the pump runs near zero delivery
Prime the pump by returning the liquid to the suction line when the pump is started
Reduce the motor voltage when the pump runs at low flow and so save electrical power
explanation: At shut-off, nearly all the input power becomes heat in the small volume of liquid in the casing.

question: If the diameter of a pipe is doubled while the flow velocity stays the same, the volume flow rate becomes about:
options: Unchanged
Eight times greater
Four times greater
Twice as great
explanation: Flow = area x velocity, and the area of a circle increases with the square of the diameter.
